claims.quote: a partial or complete loss of γ-aminobutyric acid uptake due to impaired protein trafficking is the primary aetiology.
Slc6a1+/A288V and Slc6a1+/S295L mice, representative of a partial or a complete loss of function of SLC6A1 mutations, respectively.
γ-aminobutyric acid transporter 1 protein was markedly reduced in cortex, hippocampus, thalamus and cerebellum in both mutant mouse lines.
both the total and the γ-aminobutyric acid transporter 1-mediated 3H γ-aminobutyric acid reuptake was reduced.

claims.object_text: no compensatory increase of γ-aminobutyric acid transporter 3
claims.quote: there was no compensatory increase of γ-aminobutyric acid transporter 3 in either of the mutant mouse lines.
a ring-like structure was identified only in the Slc6a1+/A288V mouse
suggesting more γ-aminobutyric acid transporter 1 retention inside endoplasmic reticulum in the Slc6a1+/A288V mouse.

claims.object_text: increased α5 GABAA receptor expression in hippocampus of S295L homozygous mice
claims.quote: a small increase in the expression of α5 subunits of GABAA receptor in the hippocampus of Slc6a1S295L homozygous mice

claims.object_text: tailored treatment options based on the expression and function of γ-aminobutyric acid transporter 1 and GABAA receptor
claims.quote: the findings from this study can help guide tailored treatment options based on the expression and function of γ-aminobutyric acid transporter 1 and GABAA receptor in SLC6A1 mutation-mediated neurodevelopmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
